starting_point: Comfort with computers, basic scripting and troubleshooting. IT support, systems administration or software development can provide useful foundations.

phase_1.label: Understand the running service
phase_1.slide: Linux, HTTP, Git and a simple application
actions: Run a tiny local web service and explain its process, port, configuration and logs.
Practise shell commands and write a setup script. Keep secrets outside committed source code.
phase_1.output: A working local service with a clear setup and troubleshooting guide.

phase_2.label: Automate a dependable delivery route
phase_2.slide: A reusable setup and automated build checks
actions: Package the service and automate build and test steps using local scripts or available CI.
Add configuration examples, health checks and a developer onboarding document.
phase_2.output: A small platform template another developer can start and verify.

phase_3.label: Test operations
phase_3.slide: Monitor health and recover from a failed deployment
actions: Simulate a service failure, inspect logs and restore the previous version.
Create an infrastructure diagram and optional cloud deployment design with explicit security and cost assumptions. No paid deployment is required.
phase_3.output: A reusable service template, failure drill and operational runbook.

portfolio: A local developer platform starter that builds, tests, runs and monitors a small service.
tools: Linux or an available local shell, Python or another familiar language, Git and optional local containers.
acceptance: A new user can start and test the service by following the documented setup.
An intentionally broken build fails the automated check before release.
A failure drill detects the problem and restores the previous version, with elapsed recovery time recorded.
first_step: Run a simple service locally and explain how a browser request reaches it.
beginner_adjustment: Focus on Linux, networking and scripting. Choose one cloud's concepts later instead of studying several platforms at once.
